title: Two-minute rule
idea: If a task takes under two minutes, do it now. To start a habit, shrink it to two minutes.
apply: Send that short reply right now. Then make your new habit its two-minute version: one page, one stretch, one set.
remind: Make it small enough to start.
who: Theo, buried in tiny tasks and a habit that never starts.

items.x: Put the mug in the dishwasher

scenes.nar: Theo's day is full of tiny tasks. Each takes under two minutes, so he keeps putting them off.

scenes.cap: tiny tasks piled up by Friday
scenes.sub: The pile feels heavier than the work.
scenes.nar: By Friday they have piled up into twelve nagging things, and the pile feels heavier than the work itself.

scenes.cap: Done the moment they show up

items.x: Put the mug in the dishwasher

scenes.nar: Now he follows one rule. If it takes under two minutes, do it right now. The pile never forms.
He shrinks his new habit the same way. Not thirty minutes of stretching. Just unroll the mat for two minutes.
